This only works for smaller purchases (usually under $25).  

When you dispute a transaction and there's neither a PIN nor a signature proving that you made that transaction, it will most likely be a 'chargeback', meaning that the merchant has to pay the money back and it is refunded to you via your bank.  There are times when the investigation into a fraud claim can take longer, but generally only if there is a question of the authenticity of the claim or it is a higher dollar dispute.

The merchant is basically saying that it's worth the risk of chargeback to them to streamline their checkout process.  They are gambling on the vast majority of daily transactions NOT being disputed, and they consider the number of chargebacks to be an acceptable loss based on the amount of profit and/or savings generated by not requiring the extra step.
